knowledge:
- key_parameters: dir.reports=Directory path where HTML reports will be written (must not already exist) ;; sample.sheet=Path to the tabular sample annotation CSV file ;; data.dir=Directory path containing the raw methylation data files ;; data.type=Type of input data (e.g., "infinium.idat.dir", "infinium.GEO", "bs.bed.dir") ;; filtering.sex.chromosomes.removal=Logical indicating whether to remove probes on sex chromosomes ;; identifiers.column=Column name in the sample annotation sheet to use as sample identifiers ;; disk.dump.big.matrices=Logical indicating whether to cache large matrices on disk to manage RAM
- alternatives: refFreeEWAS=Can be specified via the option "differential.site.test.method" for reference-free cell-type heterogeneity adjustment instead of standard methods ;; methylumi.noob=Can be specified as the background correction method during normalization
- when_to_use: Use when performing a complete, automated, or step-by-step DNA methylation analysis workflow on microarray or sequencing data, especially when interactive, shareable HTML reports and batch-effect adjustments are required.
- pitfalls: The output report directory (dir.reports) must not already exist prior to running the analysis, or the execution will fail ;; Ghostscript must be installed on the operating system to generate PDF plot files ;; Datasets imported directly from GEO (using "infinium.GEO") typically lack raw detection p-values and quality control probe information, which disables certain normalization and filtering steps ;; Large datasets can be extremely memory-intensive; users must configure disk dumping options (disk.dump.big.matrices=TRUE) and set fftempdir if RAM is limited.

workflows.name: infinium_microarray_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform an automated end-to-end analysis of Infinium microarray data from raw IDAT files and sample annotations to generate comprehensive HTML reports.
input: sample_annotation.csv (sample annotation table with phenotypic and batch information)
workflows.stages: 1. Set global analysis options (e.g., sex chromosome removal, sample identifier column) ;; 2. Run the complete analysis pipeline using the automated runner function.

workflows.name: bisulfite_sequencing_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform an automated end-to-end analysis of bisulfite sequencing data (WGBS or RRBS) starting from BED files.
workflows.stages: 1. Define the data source paths ;; 2. Run the complete analysis pipeline specifying the sequencing data type.
workflows.code:
data.source <- c(idat.dir, sample.annotation)

rnb.run.analysis(dir.reports=report.dir, data.source=data.source,
    data.type="bs.bed.dir")
